latin: Magis improprie dicitur de deo quod sit intellectus uel intelligens, quam de anima rationali quod sit angelus.
latin_note: Edelheit transcribes the same conclusion's title, from the source he consulted, with subject and predicate reversed: 'Magis improprie dicitur de Deo quod sit intelligens vel intellectus quam de angelo quod sit anima rationalis' -- 'than of the angel that it is a rational soul,' rather than Farmer's 'than of the rational soul that it is an angel' (edelheit2022:20783; farmer1998:20990).
translation: It is said more improperly of God that he is intellect or understanding, than of the rational soul that it is an angel.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch1, from Latin at farmer1998:20990
doctrine: Farmer cross-references the thesis to two of the numerical theses, 7a>5 ('Whether he has intellect') and 7a>6 ('In what way God understands') (farmer1998:12956; farmer1998:12957); this uploaded copy of Farmer 1998 includes the thesis's own bare Latin and English text but not the interpretive note that would explain the cross-reference or record Pico's formal reply to the commission (see not_established).
context: Farmer cross-references the thesis to two theses among the numerical theses: 7a>5, Vtrum sit intelligens ('Whether he has intellect'), and 7a>6, Quomodo deus intelligat ('In what way God understands') (farmer1998:12956; farmer1998:12957).
reception: The papal commission's censure of the thesis (its Q12 in the Apology's order) is recorded by Dougherty as "Wrong and can be twisted to a heretical meaning" (dougherty2008:730); a rendering of this censure in Farmer's own English was not located in the sources consulted (this uploaded copy of Farmer 1998 lacks the interpretive/trial-history notes apparatus for this thesis; see not_established). Copenhaver lists the Apology's order of the thirteen questions, giving this thesis as Q12, between Q8 (Belief) and Q13 (Soul) (copenhaver2022:436).
historiography: Beyond quoting the Latin opening of the conclusion, Howlett lists the thesis among the thirteen censured propositions without further discussion (howlett2021:2029). An unidentified German-language study on Pico's Kabbalah cites the thesis alongside 22.12 ('Conclusio secundum Porphyrium') and a thesis on the doctrine of Hermes Trismegistus, without stating an argument connecting them beyond their proximity in Pico's own text (kabbalah_paradigma:1395).
commission_verdict: "Wrong and can be twisted to a heretical meaning" (dougherty2008:730), Dougherty's translation of the commission's censure of the thesis as Q12; a rendering of this censure in Farmer's own English was not located in the sources consulted (see not_established).

quotations.text: Wrong and can be twisted to a heretical meaning

not_established: Which of the two orderings of the conclusion's Latin (Farmer's text or Edelheit's transcription) reflects Pico's original wording.
The full content of Pico's numerical demonstration referenced by the cross-references to 7a>5 and 7a>6.

A prior draft quoted the commission's censure as "false and can be taken to a heretical sense", attributed to farmer1998:21054, and separately quoted "mode of speaking of Dionysius" (Pico's alleged formal reply to the commission), also at farmer1998:21054. On verification against this session's uploaded copy of Farmer 1998, neither phrase is present anywhere in the file: this uploaded copy gives only the bare Latin and English of thesis 3>49 (near a different line, ~11704), with no interpretive note, trial-history note, or record of Pico's Apology reply for this thesis. Both quotations removed as unverifiable/likely fabricated (the "heretical sense" wording is a close paraphrase-with-alteration of the genuine, independently-verified Dougherty verdict-tag for this same thesis, "Wrong and can be twisted to a heretical meaning", which is retained). Farmer's own note on this thesis's Q12 censure and Pico's reply, if any, is not established by the sources consulted.

A prior draft cited farmer1998:23828 and farmer1998:23831 for the cross-references to 7a>5 and 7a>6, and copenhaver2022:1253 for the Apology's ordering of Q1/Q12/Q13/Q9/Q6.
